speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing; to begin our evaluation, how long do these episodes typically last, and were you able to recall anything that happened during them?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Seizures with Atonic/Myoclonic components (likely Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy given the hand gestures and age, or Lennox-Gastaut if developmental delay is present).

To confirm, does the patient have a history of developmental delays or learning difficulties, and have any EEG studies been performed previously?
